summary.text: 包 means “wrap” or “pack.” The received form is traditionally read as a pregnant figure enclosing an unformed child; another proposal connects it to a graph of someone holding a child. The character’s earliest form and origin remain uncertain.

formation.text: The received form has been analyzed as pictographic: its outline encloses an inner shape, interpreted in the Shuowen account as a pregnant figure and an unformed child. Other analyses treat 勹 as an enclosing element and a sound cue. A competing proposal derives 包 from a separate child-holding graph that first wrote 抱, but no dated intermediate forms establish that descent.

components.text: In the Shuowen interpretation of the received form, 巳 is the inner, unformed child. The competing proposal does not establish it as part of the earliest graph.
In received-form analyses, 勹 is read as enclosing the inner shape and as supplying a sound cue. These roles are not established for the earliest formation.

sound.text: In the Zhengzhang Old Chinese reconstruction, 勹 and 包 are both *pruː, supporting the proposed sound relationship in this system. These are reconstructed values, not recorded ancient pronunciations.

history.text: The selected seal-script-style image is a modern redraw of the received form, showing an outer stroke around an inner curve. It illustrates the form associated with the Shuowen account, but does not establish the character’s origin or an earlier sequence.

A competing proposal connects 包 to oracle-bone graphs traditionally read as 保, reinterprets them as a person holding a child, and suggests 包 first wrote 抱. The proposed descent lacks dated intermediate forms.

uncertainties.text: The pregnancy interpretation and the proposed descent from a child-holding graph are competing accounts; the earliest form and its graphic history remain unresolved.
Enclosure and sound are proposed roles for 勹 in analyses of the received form. The sound comparison supports the phonetic proposal but does not establish 勹’s role in the earliest formation.
The seal-script-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image, and its correspondence to a primary historical record has not been verified.

senses.period: Shuowen account; earliest attestation dating unresolved
senses.text: The Shuowen account gives pregnancy as the meaning and reads the inner element as an unformed child. This is a historical interpretation, not proof of the graph’s actual earliest meaning.

senses.period: Transmitted classical texts; written-witness dating unresolved
senses.text: Transmitted examples cited in later dictionaries use 包 for wrapping or containing, including the Shijing line 白茅包之. The date of the written witness is unresolved.
包 is used for a package or bundle as well as for wrapping and packing. The evidence does not date the development of this object sense.

developments.text: A development from pregnancy or enclosure to wrapping is plausible within the Shuowen interpretation, but its timing and intermediate uses are unknown; the competing origin proposal leaves the connection uncertain.
The package and bundle senses may have developed from the verb sense, but the evidence does not show when or how.

limitations.text: The proposal that 包 first wrote 抱 belongs to a disputed account of the graph’s origin, not an established, dated earliest meaning. Reported substitutions such as 包 for 苞 or 庖 do not establish the character’s original formation.
Later senses including encompassing, taking responsibility, and guaranteeing are recorded, but no dated sequence connects them to earlier senses.

items.tradition: Small seal script style; modern vector drawing
items.caption: A modern redraw of 包 in Shuowen seal-script style shows an enclosing outer stroke around an inner curve. Shuowen interpreted the received form as pregnancy, reading the inner element as an unformed child; the image does not establish that account as the graph’s origin.
items.alt: A black seal-script-style form with an inner curved stroke enclosed by a larger outer stroke that extends above and below, on a white background.
items.selection_reason: Clearly illustrates the received form relevant to Shuowen’s interpretation. Its modern redraw status is explicit, so it does not establish an ancient form sequence.
